report.summary: Reviewed provenance.py chunk 1 of 1; enumerated claims, found no broken claims, noted low-severity observations.
risks: line 91 | low | stdout parsing takes last non-empty line; if probe output is wrapped or prefixed (e.g., by a sitecustomize print), json.loads may fail or parse wrong line, but fail-closed catches that. | Confirm whether the probe is run with -S or a clean environment to avoid stray stdout; otherwise add a marker line.

handoff.purpose: Verify that the candidate's interpreter resolves daedalus from the candidate tree, failing closed if not.

symbols.name: PROBE_SOURCE
symbols.note: String of Python code that runs in the candidate's interpreter, prints JSON.

symbols.name: ProvenanceCheck
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass holding the result of a provenance check.

symbols.name: as_error
symbols.note: Returns a human-readable message for an evaluation void, never mentioning candidate failure.

symbols.name: _under
symbols.note: Checks whether a child path is under a parent path using resolve and relative_to.

symbols.name: check_import_provenance
symbols.note: Spawns the candidate's interpreter with PROBE_SOURCE, parses JSON, returns ProvenanceCheck.

claims.text: The evolution runner called a bare pytest, which put only each test file's own basedir on sys.path.
claims.why: Historical claim about the runner; not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: The editable install pins daedalus to the primary checkout by absolute path via an _EditableFinder on sys.meta_path, so nothing shadowed it and the candidate's edits were invisible to the candidate's own tests.
claims.why: Describes the editable install mechanism; not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The loop graded the host against itself, and every score it produced was a measurement of code nobody had changed.
claims.why: Historical conclusion about the old runner; not testable here.

claims.text: That was closed on 2026-07-29: the runner now uses sys.executable -m pytest with cwd set to the worktree, which puts the worktree on sys.path[0], ahead of PathFinder, ahead of _EditableFinder.
claims.why: Describes the current runner invocation; not visible in this chunk.

claims.text: The candidate wins by an argument about import ordering, and nothing checks the argument still holds.
claims.why: Motivation for this module; the claim about 'nothing checks' is about the rest of the system, not this code.

claims.text: It stops holding if: PYTHONPATH is set in the environment the evaluator inherits; a candidate worktree has no daedalus/ directory at all; a future refactor changes how the editable install registers itself; somebody simplifies the invocation back to bare pytest.
claims.why: These are conditions about the environment and runner; this chunk only checks the resolution result, not those specific conditions.

claims.text: In every one of those cases the failure is the WORST shape available: the tests pass, the score is high, and it describes the wrong tree.
claims.why: Describes consequences of the failure modes; not directly testable in this chunk.

claims.text: So this asks the question directly instead of reasoning about it, and a failed check voids the EVALUATION rather than scoring the candidate.
claims.why: check_import_provenance returns a ProvenanceCheck with ok=False and as_error() says 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)'.

claims.text: Those are different outcomes and conflating them is the actual bug: a candidate scored 0 looks bad, while an evaluation that could not run is unknown, and only one of them should be allowed to influence a promotion.
claims.why: Policy about downstream promotion logic; not in this chunk.

claims.text: Cheap: one interpreter start, ~0.3 s, against a suite run of seconds to minutes.
claims.why: Performance claim; not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: Run in the CANDIDATE's interpreter, cwd and environment -- not here. Reporting what daedalus resolves to in this process would answer a different question than the one that matters, and answer it reassuringly.
claims.why: check_import_provenance spawns [exe, '-c', PROBE_SOURCE] with cwd=str(base), using executable or sys.executable, not running the probe in-process.

claims.text: Reports rather than asserts, so the caller decides. A probe that exited non-zero on mismatch would be indistinguishable from a probe that failed to start, which is the distinction this whole module is about.
claims.why: PROBE_SOURCE catches all exceptions from importing daedalus and prints JSON; the probe itself always exits 0 unless the interpreter fails to start. The caller checks returncode separately.

claims.text: Whether an evaluation in root would score the code in root.
claims.why: The class holds ok, root, resolved, reason; check_import_provenance sets ok=True only when daedalus resolves under root.

claims.text: Deliberately says 'evaluation' and never 'candidate': the candidate has not been judged, and a reader must not be able to mistake this for a bad score.
claims.why: as_error returns 'EVALUATION VOID (not a candidate failure)' and never uses the word 'candidate'.

claims.text: Ask the candidate's own interpreter where daedalus resolves.
claims.why: The function runs PROBE_SOURCE with the candidate's interpreter (exe = executable or sys.executable) and cwd set to root.

claims.text: FAIL-CLOSED in every direction. A probe that will not start, times out, returns unparseable output, or cannot import daedalus at all reports ok=False -- because 'we could not establish which tree would be scored' and 'the wrong tree would be scored' have the same consequence for a promotion decision, and neither is a green light.
claims.why: Every failure path returns ProvenanceCheck(False, ...): OSError/SubprocessError, non-zero returncode, JSON parse error, import_error, and resolution outside root.

claims.text: Not necessarily fatal for the repo -- but it IS fatal for this evaluation, because a suite that cannot import the package under test is measuring nothing.
claims.why: The code returns ok=False with reason about not being able to import daedalus.

claims.text: __path__ is checked too: a namespace package has no __file__, and a candidate whose package dir lost its __init__.py would otherwise resolve to None and be read as 'no answer' rather than 'wrong tree'.
claims.why: candidates includes both daedalus_file and daedalus_path; if any is under root, ok=True.

observations.what: The probe output parsing takes the last non-empty line of stdout. If the candidate's environment injects any output (e.g., a sitecustomize or a warning wrapper) before the JSON, json.loads on that last line may still work only if the JSON is the last line; if the JSON is not last, it will fail closed. The code does not pin the output format with a sentinel.

The subprocess is spawned with the inherited environment (no env parameter), so PYTHONPATH from the evaluator's environment is passed to the candidate interpreter. The module docstring lists PYTHONPATH as a failure mode, but the code does not sanitize env; however, the check is designed to detect the resulting wrong resolution.

The check uses _under with Path.resolve() on the child, but the parent is already resolved. If the candidate tree is a symlink to an outside directory, resolve() on the child will point outside and fail the check, which is fail-closed but may cause false negatives for legitimate symlinked worktrees.
